clues: This resort town sits at the far east tip of the Dominican Republic. From here, the rest of the land spreads out to the west and south.
It stays hot most of the year, but the heat peaks in late summer and fall. That is when strong sun hits these tropic lands most straight on.
In two thousand and six, it was set up as its own tour district. It still lies under the town of Higüey and its wider province.
Its small air hub takes in more guests than the one in the nation's chief city. In fact, most flights to the whole land land here first.
White sand shores and bright blue-green seas are the sights this place is famed for. Its beaches face both the Caribbean Sea and the wide Atlantic.
